live_note: Public endpoints, measured for cost and failure only: they have no truth, so no accuracy. Each run is paced at 20 queries a minute, one at a time; its waited seconds are real time. Requests sent are the HTTP requests that reached the endpoint, retries and fallbacks included; attempts are voidx's query attempts, those answered locally included. The budget is 400 HTTP requests per endpoint per invocation, shared by the adaptive run and its rerun. A budget stop, or a down stop (the bench's, at 3 consecutive 502/503 answers or connection failures), is answered locally and never reaches the endpoint, so throttled counts only the endpoint's own 429s. "Rerun saved" is the adaptive run's requests sent less its rerun's. A live run starts in the off-peak window (00:00–05:00 Europe/Amsterdam) unless --any-time is given. The adaptive run builds on the endpoint's latest run in the shared store, so coverage grows across invocations; "measured before" is what that run had measured.
proxy_note: Baseline costs are proxy-measured: the queries, server seconds and waits the bench proxy counted between the tool and the engine. A baseline's throttling waits are real time, since the tool is a subprocess; voidx's are on a simulated clock, so they cost it no wall time.
